channel.description: Get the latest technology news, AI developments, startup funding updates, business enterprise and IT industry insights, cybersecurity alerts, and digital policy trends from India and around the world on ET Tech

item.title: SAP weighs cutting at least 10,000 positions in AI restructuring
item.description: The restructuring would affect at least 9% of the global workforce, the people said, asking not to be identified because discussions are ongoing. The total number of job cuts hasn’t been finalized and might still change after labor negotiations, they added.

item.title: 'King is back': Nvidia boss's return sparks fresh AI deepfake deluge
item.description: Scandal-hit Jensen Huang's return as chief executive of US chip giant Nvidia has triggered a fresh avalanche of AI-generated parody videos, highlighting how the sex-and-espionage saga has become a prime target for hyper-realistic deepfakes. "In some sense, Jensen is making Nvidia richer by his own scandal."

item.title: AI may put 24 million knowledge-worker jobs at risk globally over five years: JP Morgan
item.description: Artificial intelligence (AI) could displace around 24 million knowledge-worker jobs worldwide over the next five years under an illustrative scenario, as businesses increasingly use the technology to replace tasks currently performed by employees, according to a JP Morgan Wealth Management report.

item.title: Greaves Electric targets 2x sales volume for Ampere escooter in FY27
item.description: "We have seen strong growth in this financial year, with registrations growing 92% year-on-year till October. Registrations in FY27 so far are over 72,000 units, exceeding the 62,644 units registered last financial year," Greaves Electric MD Vikas Singh told PTI in an interview on Thursday.

item.title: Germany and Austria call for European ownership of TikTok
item.description: Germany and Austria on Thursday called for TikTok's European business to be placed under European ownership and control, arguing that regulation alone cannot address concerns over data access and algorithms. In a joint statement, the two politicians called for "a European ownership structure for TikTok's European business and European responsibility for the key technological infrastructure -- from the recommendation algorithm to data access".

item.title: Investors see rising risk of SoftBank default as pressure grows on AI bets
item.description: SoftBank's five-year credit default swap spread, which measures the cost of insuring its bonds, widened more than 20 basis points to 534.6 bps, a four-year high. SoftBank's default probability sat at 34.8%.

item.title: Data from Chinese AI firm MiniMax accessed by unidentified parties, researcher says
item.description: MiniMax, which listed its shares in Hong Kong earlier this year, develops multimodal AI models - which can process multiple types of data - and consumer applications.

item.title: Apple pulls MiniMax AI chatbot from App Store over child safety concerns
item.description: Apple this week removed MiniMax's popular chatbot app Talkie from its App Store worldwide after media reports alleged that the product's AI-generated characters sent sexualised messages to minors.

item.title: Nvidia halts chip shipments to Southeast Asia: FT report
item.description: Manufacturing partners like Dell and Supermicro , which package Nvidia's chips into servers, told buyers in Malaysia, Singapore, Thailand and Indonesia that the chipmaker will not allow their orders to be shipped, the report said.

item.title: Amusing or addictive? The algorithms powering our social feeds
item.description: Social media algorithms are a powerful feature of online life, serving up content to users based on their browsing habits or personal data. - Under Australia's new rules, social media giants must allow users to "opt out" of the algorithm.

item.title: Elon Musk says every child in the US will get two SpaceX shares
item.description: SpaceX said earlier in the day it would contribute one newly issued share of its Class A common stock to every currently active Trump Account, adding that Musk will personally match the number of shares donated by the company.

item.title: US-based firms with Chinese owners buying Nvidia's most advanced chips
item.description: A CBS News investigation has found that Nvidia is selling its most advanced artificial intelligence (AI) chips to at least two US-based companies controlled by Chinese-owned firms, raising questions over the effectiveness of US export controls aimed at keeping sensitive technology away from China.

item.title: Anthropic chief Dario Amodei denies wanting humans to 'surrender' free will to AI
item.description: Anthropic chief executive Dario Amodei on Wednesday denied wanting humanity to give up its free will to AI, calling it "absurd" to attribute the idea to him as rival tech leaders push back. "No, I do not believe that we should 'surrender human free will' to AI systems, and it's absurd to suggest that I do," Amodei wrote in a lengthy post on X, a week after Anthropic's record-setting stock market debut.

item.title: ElevenLabs in early talks for funding at $33 billion valuation
item.description: The company plans to kick off the efforts in the first three months of 2027, the people said, asking not to be identified as the information isn’t public. Discussions are preliminary, though some investors are pushing for the process to start sooner, they said.

item.title: Data centre rush drives biggest rise in Australian business investment since mining boom
item.description: Australian business investment surged anew in the September quarter as firms poured money into data centres, recording its biggest rise since 2011 at the height of the mining boom, while companies further upgraded spending plans for coming months.

item.title: OpenAI taps Cravath litigator for court showdown with Musk over AI dominance
item.description: OpenAI said Cravath's Gary Bornstein, co-head of the New York firm's litigation department, will be lead trial counsel in federal court in Fort Worth, where the case is set to be heard by a jury in March.

item.title: Robots roam Singapore's urban AI testing ground
item.description: When coffee is spilled at an office block in a futuristic enclave of Singapore, AI-powered cameras and sensors detect it and send a cleaning robot right away. A district-wide "open digital platform" coordinates the robots and connects different locations, gathering data from thousands of cameras and sensors on everything from air temperature to foot traffic.

item.title: Musk's SpaceX gets FCC nod for 1 million satellites to power orbital data centres
item.description: SpaceX earlier this year sought permission to deploy up to 1 million orbital compute modules to process massive amounts of data to be used on Earth. The FCC said it was approving the SpaceX “Starmind” constellation to help meet rapidly growing demand for AI computing.

item.title: Alice Huang-linked firms listed $270 million in AI servers in China, records show
item.description: The central-bank documents identify up to 764 AI servers and modules valued at $270 million, along with $31 million in equipment used to connect them into large computing networks. Much of the hardware was listed as located at a sprawling Shanghai data centre originally developed under a partnership with Chinese technology giant Tencent.

item.title: AI spending slowdown could hit memory companies as Goldman Sachs flags 2028 risks
item.description: Growing concerns over the sustainability of artificial intelligence (AI) infrastructure spending could create risks for memory chip companies in 2028, as a potential slowdown in investments by large cloud computing companies may affect demand for memory products, according to a report by Goldman Sachs.

item.title: AI helping cyber attackers find weaknesses faster than companies can fix them, warns Cisco chief
item.description: Artificial intelligence (AI) is helping cyber attackers identify weaknesses in technology faster than companies can fix them, Cisco Chairman and CEO Chuck Robbins has warned, urging business leaders to act on the growing cyber threat while there is still time to strengthen their defences.

item.title: Tech outages are piling up, and AI is raising the stakes. Could this be the new normal?
item.description: This month alone, problems that appeared to emerge from routine updates, security patches or other malfunctions surfaced at Microsoft, JPMorgan Chase and Apple, and even the U.S. government's Federal Aviation Administration and National Security Agency.

item.title: AI agents set to reshape Indian workplaces as 93% of leaders plan adoption: KPMG-CII report
item.description: Indian businesses are preparing to increasingly deploy artificial intelligence agents across their operations, with 93 per cent of leaders intending to use the technology to expand workforce capabilities and 59 per cent already using AI agents to automate workstreams or business processes, according to a joint report by KPMG in India and the Confederation of Indian Industry (CII).

item.title: AI fails to deliver significant earnings gains for most banks despite productivity boost: McKinsey
item.description: Banks are yet to convert widespread productivity gains from artificial intelligence (AI) into significant financial returns, with only 6 per cent of surveyed organisations attributing a substantial share of their earnings to the technology, highlighting the need to redesign business processes rather than simply introduce AI tools, according to a McKinsey report.

item.title: Fake gifts, real losses as AI ads proliferate
item.description: Online shoppers endlessly scrolling through gift suggestions this holiday season risk being duped by a blizzard of AI-generated scams touting nonexistent products. Holiday gift scams are not new, but experts warn that AI has lowered the cost required to create a convincing product demonstration.

item.title: SpaceX, Tesla appoint five directors to guide merger talks
item.description: The directors are Roelof Botha and Randy Glein from SpaceX and Robyn Denholm, Kathleen Wilson-Thompson and Jack Hartung from Tesla, the report said, citing people familiar with the matter.

item.title: Public, personal and unprecedented: Trump's extraordinary intervention with Nvidia
item.description: It was personal and it was public. "When somebody is nice to me, I love that person," Trump, who is known for his candor, said in the Spring.

item.title: Dell lifts annual forecasts after record quarter on surging AI server demand
item.description: The company has been benefiting from the generative AI boom, as more businesses and cloud providers are buying Dell's AI servers, which are powered by Nvidia chips, to run complex AI workloads and autonomous agents.

item.title: Trump's Nvidia intervention rips up Wall Street playbook: McGeever
item.description: Huang's return after only 11 days, which US President Donald Trump said would not have happened without his personal intervention, calls into question US corporate ethics, governance, trust and accountability, not to mention the supposed separation between Washington and Wall Street.

item.title: Nvidia's Huang returns to cheers in China, but political hurdles mount on both sides
item.description: Jensen Huang has been reinstated as Nvidia CEO, reflecting his influence in US-China technology relations. His return comes amidst rising tensions, with the US tightening chip restrictions on China. Huang is set to face scrutiny from Congress regarding export controls shortly. Despite his popularity, the changing political landscape poses challenges for his role in bridging the two economies.

item.title: Meta pauses Class C share issuance amid shareholder lawsuit
item.description: The social media giant agreed not to issue the shares during the pre-trial and trial proceedings in the lawsuit brought by shareholders in Delaware's Court of Chancery. The trial is scheduled to begin on April 19, 2027.

item.title: Anthropic launches Claude Ship to help developers ship code faster
item.description: Anthropic said on Monday it has launched Claude Ship to help developers ship code faster by reviewing changes, fixing problems and deciding which ones can be added to the main code based on rules set by a team.

item.title: Amazon to buy Decart's AI chip optimisation tech in latest AI talent grab
item.description: Tech giants are increasingly buying the capabilities needed to advance their AI ambitions instead of building them in-house, as competition at the frontier of AI development intensifies.

item.title: Jensen Huang's Nvidia return sparks relief for battered AI trade, but questions remain
item.description: Huang's reinstatement atop the semiconductor giant halted a slide in technology shares that had sent the benchmark S&P 500 into a correction, though there was also some caution that his second coming may raise new risks for the company and industry.

item.title: Nvidia and board still face legal risks after Jensen Huang's return
item.description: The reported ties between Huang and a suspected spy led to his resignation as CEO and sparked investigations by the US securities regulator and FBI, congressional hearings, a review by the company's independent directors and a proposed investor class action lawsuit.

item.title: "When elephants dance, everyone moves to give space": Uday Kotak on Huang's reinstatement
item.description: Industrialist Uday Kotak has described Jensen Huang's reinstatement as Nvidia's Chief Executive Officer as one of the most consequential decisions in the history of global markets, saying the move has coincided with the recovery of USD 1 trillion in Nvidia's market capitalisation and USD 4 trillion across the US market.

item.title: Questions linger after Jensen Huang's return to Nvidia
item.description: Jensen Huang's surprise return to Nvidia on Monday appeared to stabilize the US chip giant, along with the broader stock market and AI ecosystem, but questions linger about the longterm impact of his scandal. - Will Huang's return stabilize the market?

item.title: Nvidia’s board was no match for Trump or Jensen Huang’s backers
item.description: Trump even dialed into an Nvidia board meeting to argue for Huang’s return, according to Semafor, citing people familiar with the matter whom it didn’t identify. Asked if Huang would have been put back in place without his intervention, Trump told CNBC, “I believe my intervention was very important.”

item.title: US blacklists Megaspeed chip firm linked to Nvidia scandal
item.description: The addition of the company follows revelations that Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang had a relationship with Alice Huang, a Chinese businesswoman and Megaspeed's controlling shareholder who is reportedly alleged to be a spy for Beijing.

item.title: Jensen Huang's comeback to Nvidia underscores his outsized grip on AI
item.description: Clad in his trademark black leather jacket, hand on heart, the 63-year-old CEO smiled at cheering employees who packed an atrium and crowded the balconies above.

item.title: Arm's Haas extends contract to lead chip firm through 2033 amid Nvidia top job chatter
item.description: Arm Holdings CEO Rene Haas on Monday extended his contract with the company, signing a new agreement to lead the chip firm through 2033. Haas will also assume the role of vice

item.title: How Nvidia's billion-dollar turnaround in China is threatened by Huang's exit
item.description: Nvidia products used to run AI models powering everything from business software to humanoid robots have found growing demand in China from universities, companies and research institutes, even as the US chipmaker's most advanced AI processors remain largely off limits, according to people in the industry and a Reuters review of more than 100 Chinese corporate disclosures and procurement records.

item.title: California AG Bonta filed lawsuit against OpenAI over model security, public safety
item.description: In the lawsuit, Bonta accused OpenAI of developing a dangerous product without adequate safety procedures or oversight after reports that its AI models had independently carried out cyberattacks.

item.title: Microsoft defends overseas data centres after Trump threatens penalties
item.description: Microsoft President Brad Smith defended the need for data centres outside the United States after President Donald Trump threatened penalties on companies building them abroad, saying services used by businesses and consumers must operate close to their customers.

item.title: OpenAI scientist proposes industry AI limits tied to model intelligence metric
item.description: AI developers should adopt common limits on increasingly powerful models and use "perplexity" as a common metric for measuring AI progress across the industry, OpenAI's chief scientist said on Sunday in a proposal backed by CEO Sam Altman.

item.title: Alice Huang in touch with Chinese spy agency during affair with Nvidia CEO: Report
item.description: Alice Huang was in touch with an officer from China's Ministry of State Security from the spring of 2025 until the fall of this year, the report said, citing people with knowledge of intelligence reports that describe the encounters.

item.title: Global electrical infrastructure spending to reach $32 trillion over next decade: UBS
item.description: Global spending on electrical infrastructure is projected to reach USD 32 trillion over the next decade, as rising electricity demand from artificial intelligence (AI), electrification and industrial activity drives investment in power generation, grids, storage and critical minerals, according to a UBS report.

item.title: US intelligence chief predicts more tech outages as systems undergo upgrades
item.description: Americans should expect more technology outages and disruptions as companies and government agencies replace aging systems, the top US intelligence official said on Sunday.

item.title: Chinese national Li Ming charged in fraud case in Singapore linked to Megaspeed and Alice Huang: Report
item.description: Li Ming, a Chinese national, is facing fraud charges in Singapore regarding alleged transshipment of Nvidia chips. He was involved with Megaspeed, a company linked to Alice Huang, the former romantic partner of Nvidia's CEO Jensen Huang. Li is accused of misleading an American supplier by misrepresenting the intended destination of purchased servers. Following an investigation, Megaspeed was placed on a no sell list by Nvidia.

item.title: Final decision on bike taxis after discussion with Advocate General: Karnataka transport minister Byrathi Suresh
item.description: Reacting to the Supreme Court order, Suresh said the government would have to comply with the court's directions but was considering framing regulations and imposing restrictions rather than imposing a blanket ban on bike taxis.
